In /opt/nxeon-staging, the admin live-chat inbox needs 4 new features. This is the Nxeon VPS/game-hosting platform's live-chat system (visitor widget + admin inbox + an AI auto-responder).

## Files to read first
- `components/admin/ChatInbox.tsx` (579 lines) — the admin live-chat inbox UI (conversation list + thread view + reply box)
- `app/admin/chat/page.tsx` (75 lines) — the page wrapper
- `app/api/chat/route.ts` (242 lines) — the visitor-facing chat API; find where it decides to generate an AI reply (search for where a bot/assistant message gets created after a visitor message — likely calls into `lib/kb-run.ts` or a similar AI-response module)
- `lib/kb-run.ts` — likely where the AI agent's response logic lives
- `app/api/chat/upload/route.ts` and `lib/chat-attachment.ts` — the EXISTING image-upload pattern (visitor side already supports pasting/uploading images into chat; verify whether the ADMIN side (`ChatInbox.tsx`) already has equivalent upload/paste support for agent replies, or only the visitor side does — read the reply-sending code path in `ChatInbox.tsx` carefully before assuming either way)
- `prisma/schema.prisma` — `model ChatConversation` (~line 2623), `model ChatMessage` (~line 2653), `model ChatAttachment` (~line 2673), and `model Ticket` (~line 305) / `model TicketMessage` (~line 333) for the transfer-to-ticket feature

IMPORTANT: `prisma/schema.prisma` currently has TWO other uncommitted fields from separate in-progress work that you must NOT touch or revert: `ChatConversation.discordThreadId` and `Ticket.discordThreadId` (both have comments explaining they're deliberately not yet pushed to production, but this is a staging-only concern — you WILL run `prisma db push` which pushes them too, that's fine and expected, just don't remove/modify those two fields themselves). Also, other background agents may be concurrently editing this same tree (a scheduled improvement agent and other feature work) — before editing any shared file, re-read it fresh rather than trusting only what's summarized here, and make your changes additive rather than restructuring things other agents might have just added.

## What to build

### 1. Per-conversation "pause AI" toggle
- Add `aiPaused Boolean @default(false)` to `ChatConversation` in the schema.
- Find where `app/api/chat/route.ts` (or wherever the AI reply is actually triggered — trace the full call chain, don't guess) decides to generate and post an AI response after a visitor message. Add a check: if `conversation.aiPaused` is true, skip AI generation entirely (the visitor's message still gets saved and marked unread for a human agent, exactly like today's human-handoff/escalation path already does — reuse that "waiting for a human" UX pattern if one already exists via `botEscalatedAt`, don't invent a new one if an equivalent already exists).
- Admin UI: a toggle/button in `ChatInbox.tsx`'s conversation header (next to "Assign to me" / "Close") — something like "AI: On" / "AI: Paused" that flips `aiPaused` via a new server action. Make the current state clearly visible (e.g. a colored badge) so staff can tell at a glance whether the bot is live or paused on this specific thread.

### 2. Paste images into admin replies
- Determine current state first: does `ChatInbox.tsx`'s reply box already support image paste/upload for AGENT-sent messages, or does only the customer-facing widget have this? (The existing `/api/chat/upload` route and `lib/chat-attachment.ts` may be visitor-only — check for a `sender: "visitor"` hardcode or similar restriction before assuming it's reusable as-is.)
- If agent-side upload doesn't exist: add a paste handler (`onPaste`, detect `image/*` in `event.clipboardData.items`) and/or an upload button on the admin reply textarea, POSTing to either the existing `/api/chat/upload` route (extended to accept an `agent` sender when called by an authenticated admin) or a new admin-specific route — pick whichever avoids duplicating the image-validation logic in `lib/chat-attachment.ts` (reuse it, don't reimplement). Attachments should render inline in the thread exactly like visitor-sent images already do.

### 3. Voice-to-text for admin replies
- Add a microphone button next to the admin reply textarea using the browser's native Web Speech API (`window.SpeechRecognition || window.webkitSpeechRecognition`). Feature-detect and simply don't render the button if unavailable (e.g. Firefox). Click to start listening (visual recording/pulsing state), click again or on natural `onresult`/`onend` to stop, append the transcript into the reply textarea. This is UI-only, no server changes.

### 4. "Transfer to ticket" button
- Add a button in `ChatInbox.tsx`'s conversation header (near Assign/Close) — "Transfer to ticket" (or similar).
- New server action `transferChatToTicket(conversationId)`:
  - Ownership/auth: admin-only (same gate the rest of `ChatInbox.tsx`'s actions already use — follow the existing pattern, don't invent a new auth check).
  - Creates a new `Ticket` row. Requires a `userId` — if the conversation has one (`ChatConversation.userId`, set for signed-in visitors), use it directly. If the conversation is from an anonymous visitor (`userId` is null), decide sensibly: either require the conversation to have a matched/linked user before allowing transfer (simplest, safest — show a clear error/disabled state explaining a ticket needs an account "This chat isn't linked to a customer account yet — [find how the codebase already resolves a visitor's email/name to a User elsewhere, e.g. in `app/api/chat/route.ts`'s visitor-matching logic] before transfer is possible", OR whatever the codebase's existing convention is for this exact anonymous-visitor problem) — investigate how `ChatConversation.email`/`name` are normally reconciled to a real `User` account elsewhere in this codebase (there's likely existing logic since email/name are already stored on the conversation) before deciding, rather than inventing new user-matching logic from scratch.
  - Subject: derive from the conversation (e.g. first visitor message, truncated, or the conversation's stored name/subject if one exists).
  - Copies the conversation's message history into `TicketMessage` rows (mapping `sender: "visitor"` → `isStaff: false`, `sender: "agent"` → `isStaff: true`; `authorId` for staff messages should be the actual staff member's id if resolvable, otherwise the current admin performing the transfer — check how existing staff messages elsewhere attribute authorship), preserving `createdAt` timestamps and any attachments if the effort fits cleanly (attachments are a nice-to-have here — if the `TicketMessage`/`ChatMessage` attachment shapes don't line up cleanly and another agent is concurrently adding ticket attachments, it's fine to skip copying attachment bytes and just note "[image attachment omitted]" in the copied message body rather than blocking on it).
  - Marks the original `ChatConversation` as closed (`status: "CLOSED"`) and posts a final system-style message in the chat noting it was transferred (visible to the visitor if they return, e.g. "This conversation was transferred to a support ticket — an agent will follow up there.").
  - Redirects the admin to the new ticket's admin detail page (`/admin/support/[id]`) on success.

## Constraints
- This codebase has a standing rule: NEVER send a support-ticket reply without explicit human sign-off — this applies to you as the agent too. Build and verify the transfer/upload/voice mechanics via type-checking and logic review; do NOT actually invoke your new transfer action against any real live conversation, and do not send any live chat replies as part of testing.
- Run `npx tsc --noEmit` after schema changes and after each major piece; fix errors before moving on.
- After schema edits, run `npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss` in `/opt/nxeon-staging` to sync the staging DB.
- Use the existing Nxeon dark theme (`card` class, `white/10` borders, `brand-500`/`accent-blue` accents, `slate-400` text, `navy-900`/`navy-950` backgrounds) and match `ChatInbox.tsx`'s existing visual conventions exactly (button styles, spacing) rather than introducing new ones.
- Do NOT run `npm run build` — another process may hold the build lock in this shared staging tree. `npx tsc --noEmit` is sufficient verification.

Report back exactly what you built for each of the 4 items, key design decisions (especially the anonymous-visitor-to-ticket resolution and the attachment-copy handling), and any files touched.
